raw_docx_blocks.text: You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1-3.

Deep sea hydrothermal vents host extraordinary ecosystems completely independent of solar photosynthesis. Chemotrophic bacteria utilize hydrogen sulfide expelled from subterranean tectonic fractures to synthesize organic compounds. Giant tube worms lack digestive tracts entirely, relying instead on billions of symbiotic bacteria residing in their specialized trophosome tissue to convert mineral solutes into cellular nutrition. Early deep-ocean exploration teams faced extreme technical difficulties attempting to collect biological specimens without physical destruction, until pressurized titanium recovery vessels were introduced by marine engineers.
Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
1. Chemotrophic bacteria synthesize organic compounds from hydrogen sulfide
2. Giant tube worms rely on symbiotic bacteria for nutrition
3. Titanium canisters were used for collecting deep sea specimens
